children: Volkswagen AG Pref (XETR:VOW) unveiled a sweeping Future Plan 2030—cutting ~50,000 jobs, halving models by 2035, closing four German plants and aiming for a 9% margin—while reshaping brands, probing supplier hires, expanding North America SUVs/pickups and localising to offset $5.8B in U.S. tariffs.
: Volkswagen AG Pref (VOW): Supervisory board approved Future Plan 2030. Plans ~50,000 more job cuts, halve models by 2035, close four German plants 2031–34, target 9% margin by 2030.
: Volkswagen AG Pref (VOW) says U.S. tariff policy hits U.S. business, estimating roughly $5.8 billion annual impact; company pursuing greater U.S. production localization to reduce tariff exposure.
: Volkswagen AG Pref (VOW): political and labor leaders, including Lower Saxony and Porsche SE, backed a deal with the works council and IG Metall to avoid an emergency shareholder meeting.
: Volkswagen AG Pref (VOW): Internal memo reported by WirtschaftsWoche says VW plans to drop Seat by 2029 while retaining Cupra—relevant for brand exposure and model lineup for traders.
: Volkswagen AG Pref (VOW) signals North America plans: new SUVs and pickups under review, including possible body-on-frame B‑segment models and expanded hybrid powertrain options for the region.
: Volkswagen AG Pref (VOW): Marco Schubert to lead North America from Oct. 1, joining the extended group management board and reporting to CEO Oliver Blume; Kjell Gruner to depart the role.
: Volkswagen AG Pref (VOW) named Marianne Heiss to its supervisory board immediately and appointed her audit committee chair as the firm prepares a vote on a major restructuring plan.
: Volkswagen AG Pref (VOW) is probing the termination of 107 recent university hires by supplier Changzhou Xingyu Automotive Lighting. VW says itxamines circumstances and will act after review.

title: Weekly Recap: Future Plan 2030 job cuts and U.S. tariff impact
